name: SCORPIO
question: Do mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg improve incontinence and urinary frequency over placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder for at least 3 months, at least 8 daily micturitions, and at least 3 urgency episodes in a 3-day baseline diary.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority randomized trial at 189 sites across 27 countries in Europe and Australia
design.locator: Khullar 2013 PubMed abstract, Design; Khullar 2013 post-hoc full text, Methods and Results, Table 1; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00689104, Participant Flow; Khullar 2013 full text, Methods §2.1, p 284

verdictNote: Both mirabegron doses met both co-primary placebo comparisons at 12 weeks.
takeaway: In SCORPIO, mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg each reduced daily incontinence episodes and micturitions more than placebo over 12 weeks; tolterodine ER 4 mg was an active control without a prespecified head-to-head mirabegron comparison.

harms.label: Treatment-emergent adverse events
harms.note: Urinary tract infection: 7/494 (1.4%), 7/493 (1.4%), 9/496 (1.8%), and 10/495 (2.0%), respectively. PVR >300 mL at final visit: 1/493 with mirabegron 50 mg, 2/496 with mirabegron 100 mg, and 1/495 with tolterodine. Discontinued study drug due to a TEAE: 2.6%, 4.9%, 3.2%, and 4.4% of the respective safety sets.
harms.locator: Full text, Table 6, p 291; Results §3.3, pp 287–288

delivery.label: Study treatment
delivery.value: Once-daily oral placebo (n=494), mirabegron 50 mg (n=493), mirabegron 100 mg (n=496), or tolterodine ER 4 mg (n=495) for 12 weeks after a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in; 1,978 of 1,987 randomized participants received study drug. Adverse events and concomitant medication were assessed 30 days after treatment.
delivery.locator: Full text, Fig. 1 and Methods §2.1, p 284; Results §3.1, p 286
